2607.02459.title: Language Models as Measurement Apparatus for Culture
2607.02459.paper_summary: Language models are increasingly used to quantify cultural phenomena, but what makes such measurement distinctively cultural? This paper argues that NLP work on culture is a material-discursive practice: the apparatus -- model, data, annotation, evaluation -- participates in constituting the cultural reality it measures, rather than passively recording it. Drawing on Karen Barad's concept of the agential cut -- the contingent boundary between phenomenon and instrument -- I show that the apparatus's substantive design choices draw such boundaries, and that the boundary is entangled from the start because language models have already internalized much of the cultural material they measure. I illustrate this through three case studies on television and film dialogue (measuring structure, interaction, and deviation) and three examinations of the apparatus itself (erasure of cultural markers, attunement to historical material, and agency in an agentic workflow). This big picture analysis proposes a research program that is theory-driven, empirically rigorous, and culturally contingent, treating each agential cut as a conscious commitment, at once methodological and ethical.
2607.02459.paper_summary_zh: 語言模型越來越多地被用來量化文化現象，但使這種測量具有獨特文化性質的原因是什麼？本文主張，關於文化的自然語言處理工作是一種物質-話語實踐：這個裝置——模型、數據、標註、評估——參與構成它所測量的文化現實，而不是被動地記錄它。根據Karen Barad的代理切割概念——現象與工具之間的偶然邊界——我展示了裝置的實質設計選擇如何劃定這些邊界，並且這個邊界從一開始就交織在一起，因為語言模型已經內化了它們所測量的許多文化材料。我通過三個關於電視和電影對話的案例研究（測量結構、互動和偏差）以及三個對裝置本身的檢視（文化標記的抹除、對歷史材料的調整，以及在代理工作流程中的代理性）來說明這一點。這一全景分析提出了一個理論驅動、實證嚴謹且文化依賴的研究計劃，將每個代理切割視為一種有意識的承諾，同時具有方法論和倫理性。
2607.02459.author: Kent K. Chang et.al.
